messages:
incident-bot: paging @Eric — p99 latency spike detected for tenant 'Neptune Labs' on single-tenant pool neptune-prod-rack-3. metric: streaming p99 = 4.8s (SLO 1.0s), p95 = 1.1s. error rate normal. possible KV-cache miss surge. link: https://monitoring.redwood/incoming/2501234567
Eric: on it. grabbing traces and live tail. assigning priority P0.
Amy: I can join for runtime tracing. Eric, do we have a warm fallback model or lower-capacity variant to fail to?
Eric: @Amy good Q — we have a smaller quantized variant (rwd-small-q4) available in the same pool. planning to test fallback routing if we can't stabilize.
Jun: attaching recent request snapshots from affected host (last 10m). Looks like a small subset of requests have very long token prefixes (10k+ tokens) causing K/V cache thrash and continuous batching to stall.
Jun: snippet of abnormal prompt patterns: ```User prompt len: 10642
pattern: repeated JSON blobs + base64 attachments
headers: content-type: application/json```
Lina: CSM reached out to Neptune and they confirm a large batch import job kicked off ~10:10 UTC. They're seeing streaming stalls in their UI. They asked for ETA to restore.
Eric: first mitigation — reduce concurrency cap for that tenant from 50 -> 8 to reduce in-flight KV hot prefixes and allow worker queues to drain. Executing now.
Eric: running command: ```rdctl tenant update --id=neptune --concurrency 8 --pool neptune-prod-rack-3```
incident-bot: command accepted. change applied by eric_at_2501234590.
Amy: observed immediate drop in in-flight requests for that tenant from 47 -> 7. p95 improved to 0.9s within 30s, but p99 still at ~2.6s. Some streaming clients still seeing stalls.
Jun: collected live logs from worker-17 on rack-3: ```WARN kv-cache: eviction storm, 2200 evictions/s
WARN runtime: long-tail tokenization time: 900ms/token for very long sequences
TRACE request: id=req_6f3a prompt_prefix=9000 tokens```
Maria: can we enable prefix compression and longer KV cache retention for that tenant temporarily? Might reduce eviction churn.
Jun: enabling extended kv-cache TTL for neptune (from 60s -> 600s) on affected pool. Command: ```rdctl cache set --tenant neptune --ttl 600 --pool neptune-prod-rack-3```
incident-bot: cache config change queued (change id cc-2501234598).
Eric: also going to toggle continuous batching window down to 5ms for that pool to favor latency over throughput.
Amy: rolling that change now — small risk of throughput reduction for others in the same pool. monitoring.
Tara_oncall_next: FYI I'm taking handoff at +30m. will followups and postmortem.
Lina: Neptune asked if there's anything they'd need to do. Recommended they postpone their import job and re-run in staged chunks. They're pausing job now.
Jun: after TTL and concurrency changes, p99 dropped to 1.4s. Streaming stalls reduced, but we still see occasional 3s tails correlated with requests that include >8k token prefixes.
Eric: plan B if this reappears: move Neptune to an isolated node pool (hot-reserved) to avoid noisy neighbor effects. Ops, can we provision a hot node?
Maria: we have 2 spare GPU nodes in us-west. Provisioning an isolated pool will take ~8-12m. Starting now.
incident-bot: infra job started: provision-pool neptune-isolated-2501234605.
Amy: keep tracing on. Also adding temporary routing rule to prefer rwd-small-q4 for requests with prefix_len > 4k to reduce KV pressure.
Jun: adding prompt-length classifier at edge to tag and route. config: ```if prefix_tokens > 4000 -> route: rwd-small-q4```
Eric: deployed classifier config. Observing ~18% of Neptune traffic being routed to small-q4. Those requests show p99 ~0.7s. Good.
Lina: Neptune confirms UI responsiveness improved for most users. They still see one-off stalls when their importer emits a burst of 200 concurrent long prompts.
Eric: moving forward — keep concurrency cap, extended TTL, classifier routing. If importer bursts again, we have option to throttle ingress at the proxy for that tenant (per-customer rate limit).
Maria: isolated pool provision finished. migrating active connections for Neptune now with graceful drain from old pool.
incident-bot: migration job complete at 2501234618 (migrate-neptune -> neptune-isolated-2501234605).
Amy: p99 stabilized at 0.95s after migration. Streaming stalls resolved. No error rate increase.
Jun: saved traces for postmortem: trace ids [tr_2501234571, tr_2501234583, tr_2501234596]. Uploading to traces.redwood/2501234567
Eric: handing off incident to @Tara_oncall_next. I've documented mitigation steps and timeline. Please follow up with a crisp customer impact summary and owner for root cause.
Tara_oncall_next: taking it. Thanks all. Quick summary to paste into incident ticket: "Neptune Labs experienced p99 streaming latency spike due to large import job with extremely long prompt prefixes causing KV-cache eviction storms and continuous-batching stalls. Immediate mitigations: tenant concurrency throttle, extended KV cache TTL, shorter batching window, prompt-length routing to quantized model, and live migration to isolated pool. Result: p99 returned under SLO within ~8 minutes. Customer paused job and confirmed improvement. Postmortem owner: Jun + Maria. Action items: automated prompt-length routing for >4k tokens, per-tenant ingress burst protection, and update docs for heavy-import guidance."
Lina: I'll schedule follow-up call with Neptune + send the customer impact note. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow.
Jun: will own the root cause write-up and eval harness to repro the prefix-thrash locally.
Maria: I'll publish infra notes for faster on-call pool-provision runbook and add a dashboard for per-tenant KV eviction rate.
Tara_oncall_next: closing this paging thread. If anything regresses, re-open and ping me. Great work team. :tada:
